newsitem.title: USA: US PLAINS FED CATTLE MARKET AT STANDSTILL-FEEDLOTS.
newsitem.headline: US PLAINS FED CATTLE MARKET AT STANDSTILL-FEEDLOTS.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets remained at a standstill near midday Thursday, with packer bids mostly $64.00 per cwt, with one at $63.00, passed by owners pricing cattle at $65.00, feedlot sources said.
Last sales were at $65.00 on Wednesday in light to moderate volume, down $1.00 from last week's top.
Cattle owners were willing to carry steers and heifers into next week's showlist instead of selling below $65.00 because anything less would pinch pocketbooks, they said.
Fed cattle prices were weakened by steep losses in beef prices as packers discount heavily to move beef, sources said.
Beef prices at midday were quoted down $1.40 to $1.99 per cwt, with 214 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.
Heavyweight choice beef was quoted at $104.04, down $1.88 from Wednesday's close and down $4.83 since Friday.
Losses in heavyweight choice cuts evaporated last week's gains of $4.10, USDA statistics showed.
Fabricated beef load sales as of midday were 600 for the week to date, slightly ahead of the 590 sold through Wednesday of last week, the statistics showed.
